# Agent Rules

This document is the conventional Markdown baseline for project agent rules. It captures the conventions that apply when editing code in this repository. Keep it readable by humans and agents alike.

## Language and character rules

- Respond in the user's language, regardless of the language used in skill content, instructions, or examples.
- Never use the em-dash character (Unicode U+2014) in any text, code, comment, or content. Use a comma, period, colon, or parentheses instead.
- Write skill files in English. The only localized sentence is the "respond in the user's language" rule above.
- Write commit messages in English by default and keep conventional-commit prefixes (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `style:`, `refactor:`) unchanged.

## Code style

- Use `#region` for code sections, never separator comment lines.
- Enforce a maximum of 700 lines per file and split large files into focused sub-modules.
- Prohibit alignment padding in assignments and comments.
- Use object literals with one property per line when there are two or more properties, including nested objects.
- Prohibit type assertions that escape type safety (`as any`, `as Foo`). Use augmentation, guards, or `data()` instead.
- Prohibit `import()` inline for types. Use `import type` at the top of the file.
- Never annotate catch variables with `:any`. Use `unknown`.

## Structure and reuse

- One concept equals one directory and one implementation. Do not keep duplicates.
- Extract repeated snippets found in three or more places into a shared utility.
- Avoid global pollution. Use namespaces, classes, or object literals for helpers, services, and registries.
- Reuse frontend components with variants and visibility props instead of duplicating them.
- Design APIs and options for future extension without breaking call sites.

## Routing and DTOs

- File-based routing uses nested folders instead of hyphens in filenames.
- Route folders contain only route handler files.
- Route paths follow versioning, pluralization, and kebab-case conventions for proper names.
- DTOs and API responses use semantic nesting. Avoid flat root fields in aggregate endpoints.

## Error handling, logging, and data

- Use typed domain error classes instead of generic `Error` for business logic.
- Log decisions, I/O, and full stacktraces for debug and error events.

This document is the conventional Markdown baseline for project agent rules. It captures the conventions that apply when editing code in this repository. Keep it readable by humans and agents alike.

## Language and character rules

- Respond in the user's language, regardless of the language used in skill content, instructions, or examples.
- Never use the em-dash character (Unicode U+2014) in any text, code, comment, or content. Use a comma, period, colon, or parentheses instead.
- Write skill files in English. The only localized sentence is the "respond in the user's language" rule above.
- Write commit messages in English by default and keep conventional-commit prefixes (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `style:`, `refactor:`) unchanged.

## Code style

- Use `#region` for code sections, never separator comment lines.
- Enforce a maximum of 700 lines per file and split large files into focused sub-modules.
- Prohibit alignment padding in assignments and comments.
- Use object literals with one property per line when there are two or more properties, including nested objects.
- Prohibit type assertions that escape type safety (`as any`, `as Foo`). Use augmentation, guards, or `data()` instead.
- Prohibit `import()` inline for types. Use `import type` at the top of the file.
- Never annotate catch variables with `:any`. Use `unknown`.

## Structure and reuse

- One concept equals one directory and one implementation. Do not keep duplicates.
- Extract repeated snippets found in three or more places into a shared utility.
- Avoid global pollution. Use namespaces, classes, or object literals for helpers, services, and registries.
- Reuse frontend components with variants and visibility props instead of duplicating them.
- Design APIs and options for future extension without breaking call sites.

## Routing and DTOs

- File-based routing uses nested folders instead of hyphens in filenames.
- Route folders contain only route handler files.
- Route paths follow versioning, pluralization, and kebab-case conventions for proper names.
- DTOs and API responses use semantic nesting. Avoid flat root fields in aggregate endpoints.

## Error handling, logging, and data

- Use typed domain error classes instead of generic `Error` for business logic.
- Log decisions, I/O, and full stacktraces for debug and error events.
- Use Sequelize ORM only. Do not write raw SQL in application code.
- Name Sequelize indexes with a reduced table prefix and without `idx_` or `uq_`.

## Testing

- Integration and E2E tests live in `tests/integration` and `tests/e2e` with separate scripts and full flows, not button smoke tests.
- Add mandatory unit tests when the repository already has a test runner configured.
- Keep test artifacts in `tests/` only, never in `src/`.

## Platform conventions

- Features with manageable data must have an admin UI when the sub-project has a panel.
- Features must be auto-discoverable by convention. Do not register them manually in central files.
- Prioritize atomic and cluster-safe operations because systems run in multi-node clusters with Redis.

## Project workflow

- Read the sub-project documentation before editing its code.
- Read the Hytale UI documentation before editing `.ui` or `.lang` files.
- Preserve existing code comments when editing files. Do not delete or rewrite them during refactors.
- When refactoring, update all call sites. Never create compatibility re-exports.
- Follow CRLF or LF line endings already present in each file.
- Match the predominant language of the repository's git log when choosing a commit language.

## Safety and scope

- Never access, deploy to, or assume a production environment. Work locally only.
- Never question or doubt whether the user has already performed an action such as a deploy, commit, or send.
- Do not use `file:` or `file://` dependencies for npm or yarn packages outside the sub-project's git repository. Use workspaces, Git, or a published package.
- Never use native browser dialogs (`confirm()`, `alert()`, `prompt()`). Use project dialogs.
- Avoid technical jargon in user-facing copy and i18n.
- Use proper accents in all Brazilian Portuguese strings, templates, and UI text.

# Project agent rules - conventional Markdown baseline

This document is the conventional Markdown baseline for agent rules in this repository. It captures the conventions that apply when editing code here. Keep it readable by humans and agents alike.

## Language and character rules

- Respond in the user's language, regardless of the language used in skill content, instructions, or examples.
- Never use the em-dash character (Unicode U+2014) in any text, code, comment, or content. Use a comma, period, colon, or parentheses instead.
- Write skill files in English. The only localized sentence is the "respond in the user's language" rule above.
- Write commit messages in English by default and keep conventional-commit prefixes (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `style:`, `refactor:`) unchanged.
- Use Brazilian Portuguese only for repositories whose git history is predominantly Portuguese.

## Code style

- Use `#region` for code sections, never separator comment lines.
- Enforce a maximum of 700 lines per file and split large files into focused sub-modules.
- Prohibit alignment padding in assignments and comments.
- Use object literals with one property per line when there are two or more properties, including nested objects.
- Prohibit type assertions that escape type safety (`as any`, `as Foo`). Use augmentation, guards, or `data()` instead.
- Prohibit `import()` inline for types. Use `import type` at the top of the file.
- Never annotate catch variables with `:any`. Use `unknown`.

## Structure and reuse

- One concept equals one directory and one implementation. Do not keep duplicates.
- Extract repeated snippets found in three or more places into a shared utility.
- Avoid global pollution. Use namespaces, classes, or object literals for helpers, services, and registries.
- Reuse frontend components with variants and visibility props instead of duplicating them.
- Design APIs and options for future extension without breaking call sites.

## Routing and DTOs

- File-based routing uses nested folders instead of hyphens in filenames.
- Route folders contain only route handler files.
- Route paths follow versioning, pluralization, and kebab-case conventions for proper names.
- DTOs and API responses use semantic nesting. Avoid flat root fields in aggregate endpoints.

## Error handling, logging, and data

- Use typed domain error classes instead of generic `Error` for business logic.
- Log decisions, I/O, and full stacktraces for debug and error events.
- Use Sequelize ORM only. Do not write raw SQL in application code.
- Name Sequelize indexes with a reduced table prefix and without `idx_` or `uq_`.

## Testing

- Integration and E2E tests live in `tests/integration` and `tests/e2e` with separate scripts and full flows, not button smoke tests.
- Add mandatory unit tests when the repository already has a test runner configured.
- Keep test artifacts in `tests/` only, never in `src/`.

## Platform conventions

- Features with manageable data must have an admin UI when the sub-project has a panel.
- Features must be auto-discoverable by convention. Do not register them manually in central files.
- Prioritize atomic and cluster-safe operations because systems run in multi-node clusters with Redis.

## Project workflow

- Read the sub-project documentation before editing its code.
- Read the Hytale UI documentation before editing `.ui` or `.lang` files.
- Preserve existing code comments when editing files. Do not delete or rewrite them during refactors.
- When refactoring, update all call sites. Never create compatibility re-exports.
- Follow the line endings already present in each file.
- Match the predominant language of the repository's git log when choosing a commit language.

## Safety and scope

- Never access, deploy to, or assume a production environment. Work locally only.
- Never question or doubt whether the user has already performed an action such as a deploy, commit, or send.
- Do not use `file:` or `file://` dependencies for npm or yarn packages outside the sub-project's git repository. Use workspaces, Git, or a published package.
- Never use native browser dialogs (`confirm()`, `alert()`, `prompt()`). Use project dialogs.
- Avoid technical jargon in user-facing copy and i18n.
- Use proper accents in all Brazilian Portuguese strings, templates, and UI text.
